drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna give only the added one-fifth as the reason the owner bids first?
outcomeNote: The difficulty of the preceding unit is answered: the mishna's reason is cumulative, not exclusive.

segments.he: חֲדָא וְעוֹד קָאָמַר, חֲדָא: דְּאַיְּידֵי דַּחֲבִיבָה עֲלֵיהּ טָפֵי וּפָרֵיק לַהּ, וְעוֹד: מִצְוַת גְּאוּלָּה בָּאָדוֹן הִיא, וְעוֹד: שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ כּוּ׳.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: The tanna «states one» reason «and» there are «another» two reasons: «One» reason is «that since it is dear to him he» would «increase» his bid «and redeem it» for a higher price; «another» reason is that the «mitzva of redemption» begins «with the owner; and another» reason is that «the owner gives» an additional «one-fifth» payment and every other person does not give an additional one-fifth payment.

moves.summary: answers the preceding unit's difficulty: the mishna gives one of several reasons
moves.about: the mishna gives one reason out of several, not the only reason, so the availability of better reasons is no difficulty

moves.cueHe: חדא: דאיידי דחביבה עליה טפי ופריק לה
moves.summary: enumerates the three reasons, ending with the mishna's own
moves.about: the mishna's stated reason is the last of three cumulative reasons rather than its whole ground
